meta.title: Servers and protocols: Hysteria2, VLESS Reality and WireGuard
meta.description: How Hysteria2, VLESS + Reality and WireGuard differ, which protocol to pick when a network does not pass UDP, and how the server list keeps itself current.

title: Servers and protocols
intro: Every country in your subscription comes in two variants: over Hysteria2 and over VLESS + Reality. The app labels each entry with its protocol, and you switch between them right there. WireGuard is handed out separately, as a config for one device.

hysteria2.name: Hysteria2
hysteria2.lossBehaviour: Holds its speed. QUIC recovers a lost packet without stalling the whole stream, which is what TCP cannot do.
hysteria2.blocking: Fails where a network drops UDP outright — corporate Wi-Fi, some carriers, most hotels.
hysteria2.bestFor: Mobile networks, poor Wi-Fi, anything that loses packets.

vless.name: VLESS + Reality
vless.transport: TCP with a real TLS handshake
vless.lossBehaviour: Slows down like any TCP connection: one lost packet stalls everything behind it.
vless.blocking: Works where UDP is closed and HTTPS is open: it is TCP on port 443 with the TLS handshake of a real site.

wireguard.name: WireGuard
wireguard.lossBehaviour: Keeps its speed: a small, light protocol that barely taxes the phone.
wireguard.blocking: Recognisable by its handshake — often fails, especially on mobile networks.
wireguard.bestFor: Home internet and networks where it runs reliably, and apps that only speak WireGuard.

whySeveral.title: Why several and not one
whySeveral.body: Hysteria2 is the better tunnel almost everywhere: QUIC keeps its speed on a network that loses packets, which is exactly what a phone on mobile data does. But QUIC is UDP, and some networks drop UDP wholesale — there the tunnel cannot come up at all. VLESS + Reality is for those networks: it is plain TCP on 443 carrying the TLS handshake of a real third-party site, so a network that allows HTTPS allows it too. WireGuard is there for those who know it and for whom it works: simple and fast, but easy to recognise by its handshake, so on mobile networks it works worse than the others.

whichToPick.title: Which one to pick
whichToPick.body: Start with Hysteria2 — on most networks it is the fastest. If it will not connect, switch to VLESS for the same country: it works where UDP is closed. Nothing needs configuring: both variants are already in your subscription, and the app remembers which one worked. WireGuard is for a router or an app that only speaks it: make a config in your account or in the Telegram bot.

howMany.title: How many devices
howMany.body: One subscription covers several devices at once, and the app on each of them fetches the same link. The link is the credential, so adding a phone means pasting the same URL into it. Only WireGuard takes a config per device — on a router or in its official app.

addingMore.title: When a country appears or disappears
addingMore.body: The server list lives in the subscription, not in the app, so a node we add shows up on the next refresh without you doing anything. The same is true in reverse: a node taken out of rotation stops being offered. That is the reason to add the link as a subscription rather than as a single server.
